Density of the 17Al alloy measured by Archimedes method = 6.76 g/cm³.
Solution-treated (as-quenched, before aging) Vickers hardness of the 17Al alloy = 259.8 ± 1.5 HV (baseline of the process chain; Table 3).
Full 625 °C aging series for the 17Al alloy (Table 3): 1 h = 813.0 ± 20.8 HV, 3 h = 872.0 ± 24.4 HV (= this sample), 6 h = 878.4 ± 28.3 HV, 10 h = 870.5 ± 24.9 HV.

The peak hardness of the 17Al alloy was 924.9 ± 25.8 HV after aging at 575 °C for 6 h (not at 625 °C); the fracture toughness K_IC of that peak-hardness 17Al sample was 6.6 MPa·m^1/2, and the elastic modulus used for the calculation was 175 GPa.
For the hardest 17Al sample (575 °C/6 h), β-Mn intrinsic hardness = 12.2 ± 0.1 GPa, and SEM-EDS composition of β-Mn = Mn 36.2 at.%, Al 16.3 at.%, Cu 2.6 at.%.
The paper reports the maximum specific hardness of the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu family as 141 HV·cm³/g, achieved by the Fe-35.2Mn-15.0Al-5.2Cu (15Al) alloy — not by the 17Al sample.

No dedicated micrograph/EBSD/TEM/XRD characterization was reported specifically for the 17Al alloy at 625 °C/3 h; the 625 °C aging data for 17Al are limited to the Vickers hardness value/tabulated series and the corresponding contour plot (Fig. 2b). Microstructure descriptions used here reflect the general 17Al aging behavior at ≥600 °C.
The optimal aging temperature range for achieving ultra-high hardness in the 17Al alloy was reported as 550–600 °C (625 °C lies slightly above this window).
